title: Relief for the Business a Client Leaves in the Diary
content:
What the client still has in the diary is read on a Private Event & Banquet Services cancellation, counting the confirmed events on the agreement that have neither been delivered nor cancelled.

1. Where two or more such events stand on the agreement, the charge worked at that percentage is reduced by a quarter, because the business that remains keeps the venue whole; 75 per cent of it stands.
2. Where exactly one such event stands on the agreement, the charge worked at that percentage is reduced by a tenth; 90 per cent of it stands.
3. Where no such event stands on the agreement, the charge worked at that percentage stands as it is.

The count is taken across the whole agreement rather than the single booking, and an event that has been delivered and an event that has been cancelled are each left out of it.

| Confirmed events on the agreement neither delivered nor cancelled | What stands of the charge worked at that percentage |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | All of it |
| 1 | 90 per cent of it |
| 2 | 75 per cent of it |
| 5 | 75 per cent of it |

## Worked illustration on hypothetical figures

A charge worked at its percentage comes to 4800 on an agreement carrying three further confirmed events that have been neither delivered nor cancelled. Two or more such events stand, so the charge is reduced by a quarter and 3600 stands. Had exactly one such event stood, 4320 would stand; had none, the whole 4800.
